title: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms

source.name: Bank for International Settlements - Basel Committee on Banking Supervision

summary: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision published finalising reforms to the Basel III framework in December 2017, addressing post-crisis regulatory shortcomings. Key objectives include reducing excessive variability in risk-weighted assets (RWAs), enhancing standardised approaches for credit and operational risk, constraining internally-modelled approaches, and complementing risk-weighted capital ratios with a finalised leverage ratio and robust capital floor.
key_points: Primary objective is reducing excessive variability in banks' risk-weighted assets (RWAs), which eroded stakeholder faith during the financial crisis
Revised standardised approach for credit risk effective 1 January 2022
Internal ratings-based (IRB) framework revisions effective 1 January 2022, with 1.06 scaling factor removed
Leverage ratio revised exposure definition effective 1 January 2022; G-SIB buffer effective 1 January 2022
Implementation committed to not significantly increasing overall capital requirements based on quantitative impact study
why_it_matters: This document represents the final Basel III regulatory framework that shapes global banking capital requirements. It directly affects how banks calculate risk-weighted assets, leverage ratios, and minimum capital floors—all critical inputs to market structure and bank risk management. The phased output floor implementation (capping internally-modelled RWAs at 72.5% of standardised approach by 2027) constrains model discretion and affects competitive dynamics between banks using internal models versus standardised approaches.
market_structure_context: This document directly shapes market structure by establishing global banking capital standards. Key market structure elements include: (1) output floor constrains internally-modelled capital calculations, reducing RWA variability; (2) standardised approach enhancements affect credit risk assessment for bank borrowers; (3) leverage ratio revisions with revised exposure definitions affect bank balance sheet reporting; (4) G-SIB buffer requirements affect systemically important bank capital planning.
important_numbers: IRB scaling factor: 1.06 removed upon implementation
Implementation date for standardised approach: 1 January 2022
Implementation date for leverage ratio revised exposure: 1 January 2022
